clue.text: Dusk or thereabouts, when smokers relax?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the hour from which vehicles must show their lamps
second meaning, read literally: the moment a smoker reaches for a match

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a real British term for the time road lamps must be switched on; the question mark flags the playful literal second reading about cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighting-up time is the official evening hour when drivers must switch on their lamps, roughly at dusk.

clue.text: Tolkein's title for top male gymnast?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the name of the famous fantasy trilogy
second meaning, whimsically: the master of the rings apparatus in men's gymnastics

explanation.walkthrough: Tolkien is misspelt in the source. The rings are a men's gymnastics apparatus, so their best performer is playfully crowned their lord.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord of the Rings is the title of Tolkien's epic novel, and a champion on the rings would rule that apparatus.

clue.text: Superhuman boxer perhaps returning favour

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the word for the boxer is read backwards

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog; 'perhaps' marks it as an example
to favour something is to like it

explanation.surface: A boxer seems to be repaying a favour with almost superhuman generosity.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer is the dog breed, not a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Godlike describes powers or qualities beyond those of a mortal person, which is what superhuman means.

clue.text: Republican state stops erection of final crossing

indicators.note: to stop a hole is to plug it, so one piece is put inside another
in a down clue, erecting something stands it upright, so the word below is read from the bottom up

parts.note: final means last
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican
to state is to aver, to declare

explanation.surface: A Republican state government halts construction of the last bridge across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: LAST stood on end gives TSAL, and R plus AVER plugs its middle: T-RAVER-SAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A traversal is the act of going across something, so it is a crossing.

clue.text: Head over bank showing less stability?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
a bank is a row or tier, as of seats or oars

explanation.surface: Someone tumbling head first over a riverbank, looking rather unsteady.
explanation.walkthrough: The stability meant is mental, hence the question mark: a nuttier person is crazier.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutty is informal for mad, so the comparative suggests a mind with less mental balance.

clue.text: Elated boyfriend departs refreshed

parts.note: feeling up is feeling happy and elated
a date is the person you are going out with
D is the abbreviation for departs on timetables

explanation.surface: A happy boyfriend leaves feeling revived.
explanation.walkthrough: D for departs comes from railway timetables.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh information, such as a web page, is to bring it up to date, so updated.

clue.text: Twit supports broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the air, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: golf tees support the ball

explanation.surface: A fool backs a radio or TV transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: Twit is a verb here, not the noun for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To twit someone is an old verb meaning to taunt or rib them good-naturedly, which is to tease.

clue.text: Cosmetic mum's used to hide a blemish

indicators.note: something that hides another covers it, so it wraps around the other letters

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
taken as written
a scar is a mark or blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: Mother applies make-up to cover up a mark on her face.
explanation.walkthrough: Read mum's as 'mum is', so mum is the word doing the hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is a cosmetic applied to darken and thicken the eyelashes.

clue.text: Travelling adults, primarily, and a kid go cheaply thus?

definitions.text: Travelling adults, primarily, and a kid go cheaply thus?

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move about, so they are rearranged
primarily means at first, so only the opening letter of the word before is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of adults
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family of adults and a child travels on a budget this way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: it is the wordplay and also a description of a family going away on a bargain trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A package holiday bundles travel and lodging at one price, a cheap way for parents and children to go abroad.

clue.text: Magnificent harangue about returned benefit

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds the other

parts.note: a harangue is a rant

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: aid is help or benefit

explanation.surface: A splendid speech complaining about benefit payments that were sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: Benefit here is help in general, not a welfare payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiant means shining brightly or glowing with splendour, close to magnificent.

clue.text: Diehards seen at every other Middle Eastern tourist spot

indicators.note: every other means one in two, so alternate letters are kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and so on letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Stubborn holdouts were spotted at all the popular sights in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: The word at belongs to the letter source, not the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dead Sea, the salt lake between Israel and Jordan, is a popular destination where visitors float in the water.

clue.text: Suspended over French resort

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Someone banned from a holiday in the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: O for over comes from cricket scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan put on ice is shelved or postponed, temporarily halted, so suspended.

clue.text: Ignorant, like Noah's animals about end of flood?

indicators.note: about means around, so the phrase wraps the single letter

parts.note: the animals were in the ark during the flood

indicators.note: end of a word means its final letter alone is taken

parts.note: the last letter of flood

explanation.surface: Uninformed, like the beasts aboard Noah's vessel waiting for the waters to subside.
explanation.walkthrough: IN THE ARK goes around D, giving IN THE D-ARK.
explanation.definitionFit: To be kept in the dark is an idiom for being uninformed about something.

clue.text: Firm feeding tramp's highly thought of

indicators.note: food goes into a mouth, so feeding puts one piece inside another

parts.note: to tramp is to tread heavily
firm and sure both mean steady and secure

explanation.surface: A company that gives meals to a vagrant earns great respect.
explanation.walkthrough: Tramp is the verb to walk heavily, not a homeless person, and tramp's means 'tramp is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured is cherished and valued greatly, which is being highly thought of.

clue.text: Colloquialisms used in returning signal speedily

definitions.note: plural definition for an uncountable noun covering many such words

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read from right to left
letters used in a phrase are contained within it

parts.note: read backwards, the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Informal words are used when sending a message back quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse 'signal speedily' and the answer appears spanning both words.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is the collective term for informal words and expressions, so it covers colloquialisms.

clue.text: Sexy Home Counties channel Nutmeg's following

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the setter's piece goes at the end

parts.note: the Home Counties around London are in the South East
a duct is a channel or pipe
Nutmeg is the setter, so Nutmeg's means I've, the setter has

explanation.surface: An alluring TV channel in the counties around London, with the setter tuned in.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves by name; Nutmeg's is read as I have, I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Seductive means alluring or tempting in an erotic way, a close synonym of sexy.

clue.text: Slippery customer pocketing 10 pence in bar

indicators.note: to pocket something is to put it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an eel is a slippery creature, and a slippery customer is a shifty person
X is the Roman numeral for ten
p is the abbreviation for pence

explanation.surface: A shifty character steals ten pence in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar is the verb meaning to ban, not a pub; X and P go inside EEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel someone is to throw them out and keep them out, which is to bar them.

clue.text: Self-righteous tutor refusing last pepper

indicators.note: refusing the last letter means it is turned away and dropped

parts.note: pi is short for pious, sanctimonious
a mentor guides and tutors

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious teacher turns down the last of the pepper.
explanation.walkthrough: PI for pious is British slang. MENTOR loses its final R.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimento is a sweet red pepper, often used to stuff olives.

clue.text: Carry on with abandon — resistance ends here

definitions.note: describes the place where a last stand is made; the answer is a phrase for that final position

parts.note: to last is to continue or carry on
to ditch is to abandon

explanation.surface: Keep going recklessly until the fight is finally over.
explanation.walkthrough: Abandon looks like the noun in 'with abandon', but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The last ditch is the final defensive trench, where defenders make their final stand before giving up.

clue.text: Articles from rising editor nonsensical writer's describing

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw around something, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse; the 's adds S

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means going up the page, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: ed is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Newspaper pieces written by an ambitious editor, depicted by a writer of nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear is the classic nonsense poet, author of The Owl and the Pussy-Cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaders are a newspaper's leading articles, the editorials stating its opinion.

clue.text: Intervenes as tipped favourites slip up

indicators.note: something tipped is turned over, so in a down clue its letters run the other way

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in teacher's pets
to sin is to slip up, to err

explanation.surface: An outsider takes over when the racing tips fail and the favourites stumble.
explanation.walkthrough: Tipped favourites suggests betting, but tipped means overturned, and slip up is a verb meaning to err.
explanation.definitionFit: To step in is a phrasal verb meaning to get involved in a situation, which is to intervene.

clue.text: Injured parties move wearily

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People hurt in an incident walk slowly away exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk tiredly or reluctantly, trudging from place to place.

clue.text: Current cooking item cut by TV, radio etc

indicators.note: a word cut by another is split open with the other placed in the gap
cooking ingredients mixes them up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
television and radio are the broadcast media

explanation.surface: A cookery item on the news gets chopped by the broadcasters.
explanation.walkthrough: Current is the adjective meaning present, not electricity or a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Current means present or happening now, and immediate can mean the nearest in time, the present.

clue.text: More thirsty wino's not known to quit

indicators.note: letters that quit leave the word, so they are dropped from it

parts.note: a wino is a heavy drinker
NK is the abbreviation for not known

explanation.surface: An alcoholic is not known for giving up, and gets thirstier.
explanation.walkthrough: Wino's means wino has: DRINKER has NK leave it.
explanation.definitionFit: A drier throat is a more parched one, so drier works as the comparative of thirsty.

clue.text: Sycophants do it, but make slow progress

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to behave obsequiously to someone in power
second meaning: to move along very slowly

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses describe a creeping movement, one literal and one social.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers fawning on superiors and inching forward like traffic in a jam.

clue.text: Toff uncovered files of non-believers

definitions.note: adjectival: relating to those outside the faith

indicators.note: something uncovered has its outer layers removed, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a toff is a posh gentleman, a gent
taken as written

explanation.surface: An upper-class man exposes the records of heretics.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is a British word for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentile describes people outside the Jewish faith, and by extension those regarded as heathen or unbelieving.

clue.text: It protects part of leg and hips, surprisingly

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is unexpected, so the letters turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that guards part of the leg and the hips, unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' that seems to join leg and hips is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A shin pad is a guard worn over the shin, the front of the lower leg, in football or hockey.

clue.text: Transported insecurely, Roy's letter may end so

indicators.note: things transported are carried off and moved around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Roy's letter, carelessly carried, might sign off this way.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: a formal letter can close with the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Yours sincerely is the conventional sign-off for a formal letter addressed to a named recipient.
